source: claude-opus-5 reading of scans/chukchi-1-073.png via harness lines --sheets (6 contact sheets) and harness zoom at 2x and 6x
status: PROPOSAL — not ground truth. Provenance is #llm throughout: no glyph
status_cont: identity here is adopted, and every Tier-1 form awaits ratification.

contamination.why: 1-073 is not among the four refs CLAUDE.md records as spent (1-048, 1-052, 2-030, 1-151, plus 1-074 whose proposal was amended in place). No transcription of this page was consulted: the reading was taken off the raster before anything else was opened, and there is no committed TEI for it. This is the first page of the rebuild read under those conditions.
contamination.consequence: Adjudication of this page yields a usable blind accuracy figure. Record the edit count before amending anything, since amending in place is exactly what spent 1-074's.

notes: ALTO order is not reading order. Line 6 is the running title at vpos 614, above
line 0's body text at 724 — so 6 comes first on the page. Lines 44-46 are the
three footnotes, set side by side across the measure; ALTO order happens to
match their left-to-right order here but only because each is its own block.
Small caps flattened to full caps, following 1-074's running title and 1-151:
line 6 BOGORAS, THE CHUKCHEE, line 15 SEASONS.
Old-style figures throughout. The numeral 1 is cut at x-height with no dot and
is easily taken for the small-capital ɪ (which this page also uses, in ɪnp- and
ɪlv-); zero is likewise small, and CATMuS read both 20th as 'zoth'. Keyed as the
digits they are: the list runs 1.-12. and the dates are 20th.
Footnote markers are superscript digits, keyed as bare digits at the point they
print — trailing on lines 1, 10 and 39, leading on 44, 45 and 46. The ALTO
carries no markup and note-anchoring is a collation concern.
Curly quotes reproduced as printed (ASCII policy is Tier-1-scoped, keying spec 1).
Line 32 ends with a soft hyphen breaking 'expla-nation' across lines. Keyed as
U+002D as printed; joining is a collation concern, and English is where joining
is licensed at all.
Several lines carry isolated specks at or above x-height — most visibly before
'herd's' on line 14 and before 'not' on line 40. They sit outside the type body
and are not keyed.

0.text: The herdsmen, of course, never count their reindeer, nor are they able

1.text: to remember all their animals by their looks, as has been asserted by travellers.1
1.note: trailing 1 is the footnote marker, superscript

2.text: In the larger herds they know only the more conspicuous animals, such as

3.text: breeding-bucks, old dams, harness-animals, etc. If there be any loss, they

4.text: become aware of it only by the absence of one of them. Of the smaller

5.text: animals they take little notice, nor do they care much about them.

6.note: running title, small caps flattened. THE FOLIO IS 51 AND IS IN NO LINE POLYGON — it prints at the top right of the page, right of this line's box, and no TextLine on the page covers it. Read with harness zoom --margins, which widens to the PrintSpace and shows it. Confirmed 51 in old-style figures. Not keyed here: it belongs to no line, and inventing a line for it would put geometry in the ALTO that the segmenter never produced. It is the page's own witness to its folio, which the TEI <pb n> will need.

7.text: The Rev. Argentoff relates that one Maiˊñɪ-qlaˊul, a rich reindeer-breeder
7.resolved: Maiˊñɪ-qlaˊul = M, a, i, U+02CA, n+U+0303, U+026A, U+002D, q, l, a, U+02CA, u, l. The sort after ñ is dotless and x-height: U+026A, not i.

8.text: from the Dry Anui, tried to ascertain the number of his animals by counting

9.text: them by corrals. Each corralful was represented by a chip of wood, and these

10.text: were placed together in a glove.2 Operations of this kind were performed

11.text: by the rich Tungus for the same purpose; but among the Chukchee they can

12.text: occur only exceptionally, because every new experiment with the herd is

13.text: considered to thwart the qaˊa-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn (literally, “reindeer substance;” i. e., the
13.resolved: qaˊa-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn = q, a, U+02CA, a, U+002D, v, a, U+02CA, U+026A, r, g+U+0323, U+026A, n. THE g CARRIES A DOT BELOW, confirmed at 6x; both ɪ are dotless x-height sorts.

15.text: SEASONS. — It may not be out of place to add here the Chukchee method
15.note: SEASONS set in small caps, flattened; em dash as printed

16.text: of dividing the year. The year is divided into twelve lunar months or “moons”

17.text: (yiˊᵋlhɪn). The series begins with the winter solstice, the time of which is
17.resolved: yiˊᵋlhɪn = y, i, U+02CA, U+1D4B, l, h, U+026A, n. The i after y keeps its dot; the sort after lh does not.

18.text: marked pretty accurately. The dark interval between two “moons” is called

19.text: “moon interval” (yuˊᵋtir). The names of the months are —
19.resolved: yuˊᵋtir = y, u, U+02CA, U+1D4B, t, i, r. The i here is dotted, unlike the ɪ of yiˊᵋlhɪn.

20.text: 1. ɪnp-luˊwleñ-yiˊᵋlhɪn (“old-buck month”), from about the 20th of December to the 20th of January.
20.resolved: ɪnp- opens with U+026A, dotless and x-height, not the numeral 1 and not i. The list number before it is the old-style numeral 1 followed by a period.
20.note: CATMuS read both dates as 'zoth': the old-style zero is small and round and sits on the baseline. They are 20th.

21.text: The origin of the name is uncertain.

22.resolved: Č = C+U+030C, č = c+U+030C, both sharp wedges at 6x. rg̣ɪn = r, g+U+0323, U+026A, n — the dot below the g is unmistakable at 6x.

23.resolved: Lêˊê = L, e+U+0302, U+02CA, e+U+0302. loˊrg̣ɪn carries the same dot-below g as line 22.

24.resolved: G̣ = G+U+0323, dot below the capital, confirmed at 3x and 6x. êˊᵋlhɪn = e+U+0302, U+02CA, U+1D4B, l, h, U+026A, n.

25.note: THE LEADING '5.' IS OUTSIDE THE LINE POLYGON — this line's box starts at hpos 472 against ~414 for its neighbours, so neither the crop nor CATMuS has the number. Read off the page and keyed, following 1-074 lines 6 and 10, which strand '5.' and '9.' the same way.
25.resolved: Imlɪˊrɪlɪn = I, m, l, U+026A, U+02CA, r, U+026A, l, U+026A, n. All three are dotless x-height sorts; no dotted i in the word.

26.resolved: Taˊwtɪñ = T, a, U+02CA, w, t, U+026A, n+U+0303.

28.resolved: Nej̆ = N, e, j+U+0306. See the j-mark note below — this is the first of three.
28.note: The i after the hyphen is dotted; the sort after lh is U+026A.

29.resolved: Ñ = N+U+0303. rg̣ej̆ = r, g+U+0323, e, j+U+0306 — this line carries BOTH a dot-below g and the j-mark, and both are clear at 6x.

30.text: 10. G̣ɪthaˊ-êˊᵋlhɪn (“autumn month”), called also ɪlv-eiˊñe-yiˊᵋlhɪn (“wild-reindeer rutting month”).
30.resolved: G̣ɪ = G+U+0323 then U+026A: dot below the capital and a dotless sort after it. ɪlv- opens with U+026A, as ɪnp- does on line 20.

31.text: 11. Yaraˊučɪn, probably from Yaˊraw (“muscles of the back”), because it is supposed that the
31.resolved: učɪn = u, c+U+030C, U+026A, n. The caron over the c is a sharp wedge — compare the j-mark note.

32.text: muscles of a reindeer’s back strengthen in mid-winter. The same name, with the same expla-
32.note: line-final hyphen, U+002D, breaking expla-nation across lines 32/33

33.text: nation, was found among the Koryak of the western shore of Kamchatka in the form

34.text: yaraˊwučɪn. This month is also called by the Chukchee Tuˊr-eᵋče (“new-snow cover”).
34.resolved: Tuˊr-eᵋče = T, u, U+02CA, r, U+002D, e, U+1D4B, c+U+030C, e. The raised sort is U+1D4B and the following č takes a caron; both appear in this one strip, alongside wučɪn's caron.

35.resolved: Quˊulej̆ = Q, u, U+02CA, u, l, e, j+U+0306. Third and last occurrence of the j-mark.

36.text: The Maritime Chukchee use the same table of months. The Koryak in

37.text: different localities have different systems of names, but for the third and the

38.text: fourth month most of them have names signifying “false reindeer-birth month”

39.text: and “genuine reindeer-birth month.”3 Of course, the twelve lunar months do
39.note: 3 is the footnote marker, superscript, after the closing quote

40.text: not exactly coincide with the solar year between two winter solstices; but the

41.text: Chukchee do not care about a few extra days. In ordinary talk the names

42.text: of the months are often replaced by those of the seasons, which are much more

43.text: numerous than with us. The following are most frequently employed.

44.note: footnote; leading 1 is the superscript marker

45.note: footnote; leading 2 is the superscript marker. 'II.' is the reference, not a folio.

46.note: footnote; leading 3 is the superscript marker

j_mark.why: The mark over this j is a shallow smooth arc. The caron the same page sets over c is a sharp wedge with a visible apex — and the two can be compared WITHOUT crossing images: line 34's strip 34.1 holds Tuˊr-eᵋče's caron and line 35's strip 35.0 holds Quˊulej̆'s mark, and at 2x and again at 6x they are not the same mark. All three j occurrences take the arc, all four č occurrences (22 twice, 31, 34 twice) take the wedge.
j_mark.against: keying_spec 2.2 lists ǰ (j + U+030C, caron) in the marked-sorts row and no breve-on-j; review.PALETTE offers ǰ and J̌ and no j̆. So either the inventory is missing a sort or this reading is wrong.
j_mark.needs: The printed p. 10 key, which is book-internal apparatus and binds. That decides it; I cannot, and inferring the glyph from what the system 'should' contain is exactly what the firewall forbids. Keyed as the letterform reads and flagged rather than filed to the nearest inventory member — a silent normalization to ǰ would leave no trace that the question was ever open.
j_mark.note: keying_spec 2.6 licenses U+0306 on u and i and is silent on j; it is a rule about the obscure-vowel series, so it neither permits nor forbids this.

instrument.worked: harness zoom, new this session, replaces the ad-hoc per-page crop scripts. Deriving the box from the same line_box the crops and the review page use means a zoom is the same region enlarged rather than a second guess at where the line is, and --margins recovered two things vertical padding cannot reach: the folio 51, which sits in no line polygon at all, and line 25's stranded '5.'.
instrument.cost: Wrapping. A line sliced into strips is a line read in halves, and the first pass at 3x with a hand-set 440 px window put a body line across five strips and needed four invocations to cover nine lines. Window is now derived from the zoom to fill the display and the default is 2x, so the same nine lines came back as three sheets in one call. Escalate to 6x for one question — the shape of one mark — not as a working default.
instrument.still_open: Nothing on this page needed the raster outside harness zoom. Whether the dot-below g would have survived at 2x alone is untested: I read all four occurrences at 6x because 1-074's error profile says this is the class to check hardest, and that was the right order of operations rather than a measurement of what 2x can do.
